summary: How do I do a percentage-based canary rollout on a Hosted route?
description:
Customer question (via support portal):

"We currently have a Hosted route pinned to a model version. We want to try a new model version/config but only send ~1–5% of traffic at first and then ramp up. What’s the recommended way to do a percent-based rollout in Redwood? Is this available in Console and/or API?"

Requested outcomes:
- Step-by-step instructions for percentage-based traffic splitting on a Hosted route
- Clarify beta vs GA availability and enablement requirements
- Links to docs / troubleshooting notes

Impact:
- No current outage; customer is blocked on safe introduction of a new model version.

Notes:
- Customer mentioned they want cohort stickiness per end-user/session if possible (avoid one user seeing mixed behavior during rollout).
- They also asked about auto-rollback if latency spikes.

Support owner: Owen Phillips
Support readiness contact: Dev Patel
comments: 2025-03-21 (Dev Patel): Acknowledged. Confirming: (1) you’re using a Hosted route (not Dedicated/Private), and (2) you want a controlled traffic split between baseline and canary model versions. Also: do you need approval gates (separation of duties) and auto-pause/rollback on SLO breach?

2025-03-21 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Yes, Hosted route. We’d like the ability to ramp 1%→5%→25%→50%→100% with a minimum soak time per step. Ideally approval gates for production. Auto-rollback on high error/latency would be great. We primarily use Console but can automate via API later.

2025-03-21 (Owen Phillips): Guidance + current availability:

1) Availability (beta vs GA)
- Percentage-based canary rollouts for Hosted routes are currently in limited beta for select tenants.
- If your tenant is not enabled yet, we can request enablement; once enabled, you will see a new “Rollouts” section on the Hosted route page in Console.
- GA is in progress; functionality and schema will remain compatible, but UI wording and guardrail defaults may tighten at GA.

2) Console workflow (recommended)
- Go to Console → Hosted → Routes → select the route you want to change.
- Open the “Rollouts” tab → “Create canary rollout”.
- Choose:
  a) Baseline: current model version/config (what’s serving today)
  b) Canary: new model version/config
- Define the traffic schedule (example): 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%.
- Set minimum soak time per step (e.g., 20–30 minutes during business hours; longer for lower-traffic routes).
- Guardrails / stop conditions (recommended defaults):
  - Auto-pause or auto-rollback if canary cohort breaches thresholds on 5xx/timeouts and p95 latency regression vs baseline.
  - Optionally require approval to advance steps (requires rollout approver permission).
- Review & confirm to create the rollout. Start it when ready.

3) Monitoring baseline vs canary
- While the rollout is running, use the “Metrics comparison” view to compare baseline vs canary cohorts for:
  - Error rate (5xx)
  - Timeout rate
  - Latency (p50/p95)
  - Throughput / tokens per second (where available)
- The rollout timeline view will show step changes, approvals, pauses, and any auto-stop events.

4) Rollback / pause
- You can pause at any step (keeps split stable) and either resume later or rollback.
- Rollback sets traffic back to baseline immediately and records an activity/audit entry.

5) Cohort stickiness
- The rollout splitter is deterministic; to keep an end-user consistently in baseline vs canary, pass a stable key per user/session in your requests.
- If you share your integration details (SDK + what identifiers you can provide), we can recommend the best header/field to use for consistent cohorting.

Docs (customer-facing):
- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/rollouts/hosted-canary
- https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/safe-rollouts

If you want, reply with your Redwood org/tenant ID and the route name, and we’ll confirm whether the beta flag is already enabled for you.

2025-03-22 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We don’t see the Rollouts tab yet. Tenant ID: nsai-prod-117. Route: support-agent-prod. We also want approval gates (our ops team approves prod changes).

2025-03-22 (Dev Patel): Internal: requesting enablement for tenant nsai-prod-117. Also confirming whether “rollout-approver” role is enabled for their org. Looping in release/change management to make sure the kill switch is documented for this tenant.

2025-03-22 (Owen Phillips): Confirmed you’re not enabled yet. We’ve put in an enablement request for nsai-prod-117.

On approvals: once enabled, you can configure the rollout to require approval to advance steps (e.g., after 1% soak completes, it will wait for an approver to advance to 5%). We can also help you map the correct Console roles so only your ops team can approve.

ETA: typically same business day for beta enablement; we’ll update here once complete.

2025-03-23 (Owen Phillips): Enablement complete for nsai-prod-117. Please refresh Console and check Hosted → Routes → support-agent-prod → Rollouts.

RBAC notes:
- To create/start rollouts: Route Admin (or equivalent)
- To approve step changes when approval gates are enabled: Rollout Approver

If you share the emails of the users who should have the approver role (or your IdP group name if using SSO), we can help validate the mapping.

2025-03-24 (Customer - Northstar Support AI): We see it now. We created a rollout and can set the step schedule + soak time and approvals. This is exactly what we needed. We’ll follow the docs for cohort stickiness. Thanks!
resolution: Provided step-by-step guidance for percentage-based Hosted canary rollouts in Console, clarified beta vs GA availability, and enabled the feature flag for tenant nsai-prod-117. Shared customer-facing docs links and RBAC requirements for approval gates. Customer confirmed successful setup and closed the request.
